Consider the following initial value problem for the functions $y=y(x),z=z(x),w=w(x):$

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}=4-y-2z,\, & y(0)=1 \\ {z}^{′}=x+w,\, & z(0)=1 \\ {w}^{′}=y+z,\, & w(0)=0\end{aligned}
$$

We wish to approximate the solution using Euler's method.
What entries should be placed in the columns for $Δy,$ $Δz,$ and $Δw$ in the table below if the step size is $Δx=\frac{1}{2}?$

| $x$ | $y$ | ${y}^{′}$ | $Δy$ | $z$ | ${z}^{′}$ | $Δz$ | $w$ | ${w}^{′}$ | $Δw$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ |  |  | {{field-1}} |  |  | {{field-2}} |  |  | {{field-3}} |

Therefore, $y\,(\frac{1}{2})≈$
{{field-4}},
$z\,(\frac{1}{2})≈$
{{field-5}},
and $w\,(\frac{1}{2})≈$
{{field-6}}.
